correctness.rationale: For odd r≥3 and m=rk, τ swaps m pairs in a 2m-point ground set. An invariant geometric point has constant barycentric coefficients on τ-orbits of r-hyperedges. Odd r forbids a τ-fixed hyperedge; an admissible orbit has E∩τE=∅ and exactly one point from each of r ground pairs, so its support is an r-label block B and its phase is a binary transversal modulo complement, of size Q_B=2^{r−1}. Compatible hyperedge orbits have disjoint supports, giving a PL homeomorphism of the fixed set to uniform vertex inflation of the complete r-uniform matching complex on m labels. A top simplex selects a perfect partition P into k r-blocks; deleting one block uniquely identifies that P, so top relative boundary splits over partitions. The augmented tensor complex for each set of phase choices has top boundary kernel ⊗_{B∈P}ker(Z[Q_B]→Z), integrally without torsion. Top homology equals that kernel since dim k−1; rank ((rk)!/(r!)^k k!)(2^{r−1}−1)^k and W=C2 wr Sm action is induced from block stabilizer with sign of permuting oriented simplex blocks. For k=1 reduced augmentation gives q−1, and τ acts trivially on complement-identified phase classes. No lower homology classification asserted.
